column3: Affirms that Allah alone is God, adding divine oneness to the focus's self-declaration.
Commands believers to worship Allah alone, closely extending the focus's direct summons to worship.
Its abundant remembrance belongs to Moses's preparation for the divine encounter, though it does not name prayer.
Explicitly joins establishing prayer with remembrance of Allah and gives prayer a restraining moral function.
Begins the fire-and-guidance encounter that the focus transforms into attentive worship.
Maintains prayer amid changing circumstances, extending the focus's command into sustained communal practice.
Commands recurring prayer and calls it a remembrance, adding its timed rhythm and corrective effect.
The magicians' prostration and confession show embodied submission within the Moses narrative.
Places established prayer within an ongoing pattern of almsgiving and obedience after a failed obligation.
States the prophetic continuity of no deity but Allah and worship directed to Him alone.
The bare identification of a clear book does not clarify exclusive worship, prayer, or remembrance.
Closely pairs remembrance of the Lord's name with prayer as its enacted response.
Commands worship of Allah alone, while its warning-and-glad-tidings frame adds less than the closer parallels.
Immediately continues the divine call to Moses that culminates in the focus's self-disclosure and command.
The lexical overlap concerns males rather than remembrance and offers no relevant neighbour relation.
Repeats no deity but Allah and makes it a revealed warning that calls for reverent response.
Moses's request for a helper does not materially clarify the worship command.
Recitation as remembrance gives only a broad devotional resonance after stronger prayer-and-remembrance pairings.
Affirms one God and directs people straight toward Him, supplying a secondary response to divine uniqueness.
Public vindication through witnesses standing does not clarify the focus's prayer or remembrance.
Identifies a continuing community of worshippers, but adds less than explicit commands to establish prayer.
Combines sincere worship of Allah with establishing prayer, making a compact practical parallel.
The immediate declaration that Allah is Moses's Lord supplies the sacred setting for the focus's self-identification.
Standing by testimony is not a useful clarification of standing prayer or remembrance.
Links holding to scripture with establishing prayer, extending worship into enduring reform.
Allah's not forgetting gives a distant same-narrative contrast to the human remembrance commanded in the focus.
Prayer and almsgiving appear as part of righteous conduct, but the formula is redundant here.
Allah's assurance of presence, hearing, and sight supports the direct address within the Moses encounter.
Connects remembrance of Allah in every posture with the restoration of prayer at its fixed times.
Specifies humble inward attentiveness in prayer, adding a quality of the enacted worship.
Calling to Allah and declaring submission is devotional background rather than a close prayer-and-remembrance parallel.
Immediately precedes the focus by commanding Moses to listen to the revelation that follows.
The parable of carrying scripture without acting on it is not a close neighbour to this command.
Joins worship of Allah alone and established prayer within a covenantal pattern of social duties.
The prostration scene supplies only a broad same-surah image of obedience.
Restates established prayer with almsgiving and obedience, but is less focused than the earlier direct parallels.
The exclusive-deity confession in repentance adds a penitential use of the focus's monotheistic formula.
The magicians' deceptive ropes do not clarify worship, prayer, or remembrance.
Standing before the Lord on judgment day is not a close neighbour to established prayer.
Rejects worship of all beings besides Allah, providing a clear boundary for the focus's exclusive worship.
Links one Lord with one community commanded to worship Him, adding a communal dimension.
Commands preserving prayers and standing devotedly before Allah, specifying disciplined maintenance.
Presents remembrance as dependent on Allah's will and joined to reverence and forgiveness.
Directly commands the household to maintain prayer patiently and grounds it in divine provision.
Night recitation and prostration portray a community whose worship is sustained in practice.
Describes remembrance as requiring an attentive heart and listening, a secondary condition of reception.
Its reference to the earlier remembrance in scripture does not add much to the focus's devotional command.
Noah's warning to his people supplies no focused relation to worship, prayer, or remembrance.
The upright religion and rejection of association give only broad background to exclusive worship.
The dispute over Israel's division does not clarify the focus command.
The failure to belong to worshippers supplies a consequential contrast to the commanded prayer.
Abraham's disavowal of false worship is a secondary negative boundary for worship of Allah alone.
The Prophet's prior non-reading and non-writing do not clarify this worship command.
Shows that prayer is understood to challenge inherited worship and unbounded economic conduct.
Its reminder drawn from the life cycle of vegetation is only a broad instance of recollection.
Pharaoh's threat after the magicians believe does not clarify the focus's devotional command.
The command to remind believers supports remembrance generally but does not add a prayer-specific relation.
Dietary restrictions and their exception do not form a useful neighbour relation.
Commands worship and perseverance while denying any namesake to the Lord of all creation.
Warns that the identity of prayer can be hollow, adding a moral boundary to its establishment.
Seeks an enduring identity of establishing prayer for oneself and one's descendants.
Immediately follows the focus with the coming Hour and recompense, supplying its accountability horizon.
Forgetting remembrance is part of a ruinous history, a distant negative consequence of neglect.
Joins following revelation, no deity but Allah, and turning away from association.
The drowning of deniers does not clarify the focus's worship or remembrance.
Makes remembrance a response a person may choose, adding the question of receptive agency.
Concise affirmation of one God and no deity besides Him reinforces the focus's exclusive divine identity.
Moses's rescue as an infant does not materially clarify the command to worship and pray.
Remembering a bestowed favor is a different, more specific use of remembrance.
Makes prayer and almsgiving a lifelong charge, extending established worship across life and place.
Universal prostration expands the bodily submission implied by worship to all creation.
Shows that reverent receptivity issues in remembrance, complementing the prayer-remembrance sequence nearby.
Repeats Allah's exclusive divinity later in the same surah and adds His all-encompassing knowledge.
The demand to release Israel and follow guidance does not clarify the focus's devotional content.
Contrasts following revealed guidance with following protectors besides Allah, with only a limited remembrance link.
Commands sincere worship of Allah, a direct but more general parallel to the focus.
The angels' prostration to Adam is only a remote image of obedient bodily submission.
Night rising suggests devotional discipline but does not itself specify prayer or remembrance.
Combines no deity but Allah with calling upon Him in sincere devotion.
Its warning against obeying a human messenger does not clarify the focus command.
Explains that remembrance of Allah settles believing hearts, giving the focus's remembrance its inward effect.
Describes being led away from remembrance, a clear negative counterpart to maintaining it.
Repeats the direct command to worship Allah and identifies it as the straight path.
Uses remembrance to distinguish the Creator from what cannot create, grounding exclusive worship.
Affirms no deity but Allah and adds believerly reliance as a response.
The warning to Moses to flee a plot does not clarify worship, prayer, or remembrance.
Remembering Israel's favor has only a limited relation to remembrance of Allah through prayer.
Restates no deity but Allah and adds praise, judgment, and return to Him.
A settlement standing or cut down does not illuminate established prayer.
Refusal to remember supplies a direct negative boundary, though it adds little beyond stronger contrasts.
The announcement of Allah's forgiveness and mercy does not form a focused neighbour relation.
Prescribed days of remembering Allah give a limited ritual parallel after stronger prayer-based evidence.
Its emphasis on God-conscious intent and magnifying Allah is devotional but not a close prayer or remembrance parallel.
Directly contrasts the focus's remembrance with the constricted life and blindness of turning away from it.
Repentance and righteous action give only general return-to-Allah background.
Commands establishing prayer and reverence before the One to whom all will be gathered.
The Quran's extraordinary hypothetical effects and divine command do not clarify the focus.
Remembrance of one's striving on the final day gives an accountability-related extension.
Household etiquette around the Prophet does not form a relevant neighbour relation.
Joins prayer with all rites, life, and death as wholly devoted to Allah.
Commands people to worship their creating Lord, supplying a foundational summons to worship.
Commands remembering Allah and gratitude, directly expanding the focus's purpose of remembrance.
Its declaration that there is no deity but Him is a central parallel to the focus's exclusive divine identity.
Allah's own witness that none is worthy of worship but Him reinforces the focus's self-declaration.
Commands abundant remembrance and regular glorification, directly paralleling the focus's remembrance purpose.
Commands worship of Allah without association, giving the exclusive worship command its explicit boundary.
Jesus's call to worship Allah, his Lord and theirs, directly restates exclusive worship under divine lordship.
Names remembrance of Allah and prayer as practices Satan seeks to obstruct.
Joins no deity but Allah with the direct command to worship Him.
Commands upright devotional orientation and worship, adding a bodily dimension to the focus's service.
Commands inward, humble, and continual remembrance of the Lord.
Portrays those near Allah as glorifying and prostrating to Him without arrogance.
Shows believing hearts responding when Allah is remembered, adding an inward effect of remembrance.
Describes those who maintain places of worship through prayer, almsgiving, and fear of Allah.
Places prayer and almsgiving within the mutual duties of believing men and women.
Commands Moses and his people to establish prayer in their homes under oppression.
Forbids setting another deity beside Allah, providing a doctrinal boundary for the focus's exclusivity.
Commands prayer at its appointed spans, extending the focus's establishment of prayer into a daily rhythm.
Opposes a heedless heart to persevering remembrance of the Lord among devoted worshippers.
Describes Ishmael as commanding his people to pray and give alms.
Contrasts the focus's established prayer with successors who neglected prayer and followed desire.
Joins worship of Allah with the revealed duty to establish prayer and give alms.
Names establishing prayer among the practices of a community granted authority.
Commands bowing, prostration, and worship of the Lord as embodied service.
Commends believers who carefully preserve their prayers.
Declares Allah as the one Lord and commands worship and reverence toward Him.
Praises people whom trade does not distract from remembering Allah or establishing prayer.
Extends praise and prayer to all beings in the heavens and earth.
Links worship without association to establishing prayer and giving alms.
Pairs establishing prayer and almsgiving with certainty in the Hereafter.
Commands worship of Allah and gratitude to Him rather than false objects of worship.
Combines turning to Allah, reverence, establishing prayer, and rejection of association.
Commands establishing prayer alongside moral responsibility and patient endurance.
Portrays believers responding to reminders with prostration and praise.
Commands believers to remember Allah abundantly.
Directly commands worship of Allah and identifies it as the straight path.
Commands worship of Allah with religion made sincerely His.
Commands worship of Allah alone and gratitude to Him.
Commands calling upon Allah with religion made sincerely His despite disbelievers' objection.
Defines the creation of jinn and humankind in terms of worship of Allah.
Commands prostration and worship of Allah as the passage's final response.
Calls believers to let their hearts become humble at Allah's remembrance.
Warns against forgetting Allah, the negative counterpart to prayer maintained for His remembrance.
Commands leaving trade for the Friday call to prayer and remembrance of Allah.
Commands abundant remembrance of Allah after the congregational prayer.
Warns believers not to let wealth or children distract them from Allah's remembrance.
Forbids invoking anyone alongside Allah in places of worship.
Commands remembering the Lord's name morning and evening.
Commands night prostration and prolonged glorification of Allah.
Its refusal to worship others supplies a boundary case for exclusive devotion.
The concise declaration that Allah is one is a core monotheistic parallel to the focus.
